readMe: Every anon-executable, non-trigger SECURITY DEFINER function in `public` must appear in `entries` or `registeredFindings`. The class vocabulary, the finding kinds, and what each means and how it is checked live in tests/helpers/definer-allowlist.mjs (CLASSES, FINDING_KINDS); tests/definer-grants.test.mjs checks each claim against the function's latest body and fails on a missing, stale or doubly-listed name. A body with a comparison against auth.uid() that a NULL uid skips (the NULL-logic guard, nullLogicFlags in tests/helpers/definer-model.mjs) must be fixed, registered as a `gate-skipped-for-anon` finding, or carry `nullLogic: { fingerprint, why }` in its entry, the fingerprint being the body's so an edit re-opens it. scripts/definer-live-diff.mjs applies the same accounting to the live catalog.

accept_commitment.note: Flips the caller's own proposed commitment to active (`user_id = auth.uid()`); a signed-out call updates no row.

add_hydration.note: Adds to the caller's own daily snapshot row; raises `not authenticated` when auth.uid() is null.

add_meal_macros.note: Accumulates macros into the caller's own daily snapshot; raises when auth.uid() is null.

award_activity.note: Awards points for the caller's own logged activity (`user_id = v_uid`); returns when auth.uid() is null.

award_checkin_points.note: Awards the caller's own weekly check-in; the ledger row's user is always auth.uid().

award_community_post.note: Awards only for a post the caller authored (`author_id = auth.uid()`).

award_habit.note: Awards only for the caller's own habit completion; the ledger user is auth.uid().

award_meal_log.note: Awards the caller a hard-coded +10 for their own meal log, clamped to their own today; returns when auth.uid() is null.

award_momentum_bonus.note: Awards the caller's own momentum bonus; the amount is computed server-side from the caller's history.

award_my_goal_milestones.note: Reads the caller's own goals and weigh-ins and awards the caller's own milestones.

award_step_points.note: Awards points from the caller's own step snapshots.

award_tier_bonuses.note: Awards the caller's own tier bonuses from their own ledger total.

award_workout_session.note: Awards the caller a hard-coded +10 for their own workout on their own today; amount and category are fixed in the body.

can_access_conversation.note: Boolean: may the CALLER open this conversation (participant, client or owning coach); false for a signed-out caller.

can_access_workout_session.note: Boolean about the caller's own access to a session (its client or its provider's owner).

can_view_community_post.note: Boolean: may the CALLER see this post; public and profile-audience posts read true for anyone, every other audience keys on auth.uid().

channel_unread.note: Unread counts for the caller's own channel memberships only.

check_rate_limit.note: The search rate-limit primitive (2026-08-29), granted to anon by design because the Edge proxy's anon client must reach it: refuses the reserved `self:` namespace, then delegates to _rate_limit_bump, which no client role can execute. A caller can name any other bucket key.

compute_momentum.note: Computes the caller's own momentum score; returns 0 when auth.uid() is null.

consume_ai_proposal.note: Consumes a one-time AI nonce recorded against the caller (`actor_id = auth.uid()`); raises when signed out.

create_channel.note: Creates a channel owned by the caller; raises `Authentication is required` when auth.uid() is null.

dm_unread.note: Unread counts for the caller's own conversation participations only.

get_client_checkins.note: Rows only when is_coach_on_client(p_user_id) holds; anon and non-coaches get an empty set.

get_client_goals.note: Returns null unless is_coach_on_client(p_user_id), and honours the client's `share` opt-out.

get_client_penalties.note: Penalty rows for p_uid only when is_coach_on_client(p_uid) holds.

get_coach_certs.note: Approved certification type and number of a VERIFIED coach for the public coach profile (2026-06-19-coach-certs-public); unverified providers and unapproved rows are filtered in the body.

get_coach_sale_plans.note: A coach's PUBLISHED plans for the storefront, including each plan's detail jsonb; unpublished plans are filtered in the body. Owner question, not a finding: the migration's aim was a media preview, but `detail` is the whole plan and anyone can read it unpurchased; intended? (as is by_user)

get_coach_sale_plans_by_user.note: The same storefront read keyed by the coach's user id; published plans only.

get_coach_scores.note: A derived integer score per provider id (at most 200 ids) for public coach cards; exposes no raw counts.

get_coach_waitroom.note: Returns a waiting room only to the coach who owns the provider row (`owner_id = auth.uid()`); anyone else gets `not your waiting room`.

get_follow_stats.note: Accepted follower and following counts of any profile, as shown on public profiles; the caller's own follow flags key on auth.uid() and read false when signed out. Counts are returned for private profiles too.

get_follow_suggestions.note: Suggestions computed from the caller's own follow graph (`auth.uid()`); a signed-out call matches no candidate.

get_market_plans.note: The plan marketplace: published, priced coach plans with the coach display name (limit 60).

get_member_playlists.note: A member's public playlists, shown only when their profile is not private (`shape_profile_visibility`); the caller's own playlists always.

get_my_lift_prs.note: Lift PRs from the caller's own set logs (`client_id = auth.uid()`).

get_my_points_balance.note: Sum of the caller's own score ledger.

get_my_store_credit.note: The caller's own wallet: delegates to get_store_credit_for(auth.uid()), which is service_role only.

get_my_waitlists.note: The caller's own waitlist entries (`client_id = auth.uid()`).

get_or_create_coach_coach_conversation.note: Requires the caller to be a coach on the client (inline subscription and owner check on auth.uid()); raises otherwise.

get_or_create_member_conversation.note: Opens a DM between the caller and another member; raises when auth.uid() is null.

get_public_profile.note: The public profile card: returns what the target's profileVisibility allows this caller to see (a locked card for friends/private). Its migrations grant it to authenticated only, so anon reaches it through the default ACL; the 2026-08-04 migration lists it among the public name/avatar surfaces.

get_radio_song_social.note: Reaction counts and the latest 40 comments (id, author name, body, time) for a radio song key; the caller's own vote keys on auth.uid().

get_roster_weekend_split.note: Restricts the requested client ids to clients the caller coaches (inline subscription join on `owner_id = auth.uid()`); a signed-out call matches none.

invite_from_waitlist.note: Only the coach who owns the provider row may invite (`owner_id = auth.uid()`); anyone else raises.

is_channel_host.note: Boolean about the caller's own host role.

is_channel_member.note: Boolean about the caller's own membership.

is_coach_on_client.note: The authorization primitive itself: true only when auth.uid() owns an active provider row the client is subscribed to; pinned to pg_temp last since 2026-08-02.

is_discipline_coach_on_client.note: The discipline-scoped twin of is_coach_on_client, keyed on auth.uid().

is_public_channel.note: Boolean: is this channel id public. An RLS helper the channel policies call, granted by no migration; it discloses nothing the public channel rows do not.

is_username_available.note: Boolean handle availability, needed by signed-out sign-up and granted to anon on purpose (2026-06-09-usernames.sql); a handle enumeration oracle by design.

list_follow_requests.note: Pending follow requests addressed to the caller (`following_id = auth.uid()`).

nullLogic.why: A language sql body, so there is no reject to write: the comparison is a JOIN filter. `me.user_id = auth.uid()` is an inner join, so a signed-out caller (NULL uid) matches no participant row and the function returns nothing; `other.user_id <> auth.uid()` only narrows rows that survived that join.

log_ai_action.note: Logs against the caller; a target other than the caller requires is_coach_on_client(target). Raises when signed out.

mark_ai_action_undone.note: The action's actor, or a coach on its target (is_coach_on_client), may mark it undone; raises when signed out.

mark_channel_read.note: Updates only the caller's own membership row.

mark_conversation_read.note: Updates only the caller's own participant row.

notify_grocery_list.note: Returns unless is_coach_on_client(p_client) holds; notifies only that client.

post_coach_cosign.note: Requires is_coach_on_client(the post's author) and refuses the caller's own post; raises when signed out.

redeem_store_item.note: Spends the caller's own points; the price comes from store_catalogue server-side; raises `not_authenticated` when signed out.

redeem_store_order.note: As redeem_store_item, for a basket; raises `not_authenticated` when signed out.

release_ai_proposal.note: Deletes only the caller's own nonce (`actor_id = auth.uid()`).

replace_provider_licenses.note: Replaces the caller's own licence rows; raises when signed out.

respond_follow_request.note: Accepts or declines requests addressed to the caller (`following_id = me`); raises when signed out.

revoke_habit.note: Removes the caller's own habit-completion ledger row.

set_channel_pinned.note: Pins a channel for the caller only; raises when signed out.

set_commitment.note: The caller sets their own (active), or a coach on the client (is_coach_on_client) proposes one; anyone else is refused.

set_metric_source.note: The caller's own metric source, or a client's when is_coach_on_client holds; rejects a null auth.uid() first (2026-06-30).

set_my_username.note: Sets the caller's own handle; raises `not_signed_in` when auth.uid() is null.

set_program_detail.note: The client themself, or the coach for that discipline (is_discipline_coach_on_client); rejects a null auth.uid() first (2026-06-30).

shape_leaderboard_me.note: Returns only the caller's own rank row (`where user_id = auth.uid()`).

toggle_follow.note: Follows or unfollows on behalf of the caller only; raises when signed out.

track_event.note: Analytics events from a fixed name whitelist, DELIBERATELY callable by anon (2026-07-27-session-rpe.sql: it binds auth.uid() itself and rejects unknown names); user_id is NULL when signed out. p_props is caller-supplied jsonb with no size or rate cap, so anon can write arbitrary rows to analytics_events.

waive_penalty.note: Only a coach on the client (is_coach_on_client) may waive; anyone else gets `not_coach`.

registeredFindings.name: get_follow_list
registeredFindings.exposed: For ANY user id: id, full name, role and follow date of up to 200 accepted followers or followees, whatever that profile's visibility setting says (public, friends or private). No auth.uid() and no shape_profile_visibility check in the body; granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-08-follow-requests.sql:101).
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: This change is the audit and its tripwire, and writes no migration. The website profile pages call it too (livingProfilePage.jsx, memberProfile.jsx), and whether signed-out visitors are meant to see follower lists is not something the migrations settle.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: Gate it on shape_profile_visibility(p_user_id) (public: anyone; friends or private: the owner or an accepted follower) and decide whether a signed-out visitor may see follower lists at all. Dropping the anon grant is the smaller change.

registeredFindings.name: get_active_now
registeredFindings.exposed: User id, kind (workout or cooking), full name, role, lifetime points, avatar and start time of every member currently mid-workout or cooking (at most 50). No per-member opt-out is consulted, unlike the leaderboard's `leaderboard = off`. Granted `to anon, authenticated` by name (2026-06-09-get-active-now.sql:38).
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: It is a documented product surface: the 2026-08-04 migration calls it "granted to anon" and the War Room records the "Training now" presence rail as live with the function "granted anon+authenticated". Removing anon changes the product, which is an owner call and needs a migration this change does not write.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: Keep anon access on purpose (then move it to public-by-design with that note), or require sign-in, or add an opt-out the body honours.

registeredFindings.name: shape_profile_visibility
registeredFindings.exposed: 'public', 'friends' or 'private' for any user id, and 'public' for an id that does not exist (the body defaults it). A privacy-setting oracle: low sensitivity, but nothing calls it directly from the app or website; it exists for other definers (toggle_follow, get_member_playlists and the PR wall). Granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-08-follow-requests.sql:31).
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. Definers call it as their owner, so a client revoke would not break them, but that is an assumption to check against the RLS policies before the grant changes.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: Revoke it from public and anon (authenticated kept), after confirming no RLS policy evaluates it for a signed-out role.

registeredFindings.name: get_active_activities
registeredFindings.exposed: User id, kind and start time of every unexpired activity row, with no cap and no gate. The table's own read policy is `to authenticated` ("any signed-in user, so others can see the dot"), so the definer opens to anon what the table keeps signed-in. Granted `to authenticated, anon` by name (2026-06-09-user-activity.sql:42).
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. The only caller found is the mobile app (shapeBackend.js startActivity), which returns unless a user is signed in.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: Revoke it from public and anon and keep authenticated. get_active_now already serves the signed-out rail, if the owner keeps that.

registeredFindings.name: shape_leaderboard
registeredFindings.exposed: User id, full name, avatar url, points and rank for up to 200 members who have not set the leaderboard opt-out (the default is shown). This is the league mistake again, the fourth time this repo has shipped it: both leaderboard migrations write `revoke all ... from public; grant execute ... to authenticated`, which leaves the default explicit anon grant standing.
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. The only caller, src/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts, returns 401 before it calls the function, so no known caller needs anon.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: revoke execute on function public.shape_leaderboard(text, integer) from anon (authenticated stays).

registeredFindings.name: get_health_sources
registeredFindings.exposed: For ANY user id passed as p_user_id, with no account: that user's health observations (snapshot date, metric, source, value and time for sleep, recovery, HRV, resting and average heart rate, strain, workout minutes, calories and steps) for the last p_days days, which has no upper bound so it is the whole history, plus their metric_source_overrides. Both tables are owner-only under RLS, so the definer opens to the internet what RLS locks. The body reads `if v_uid <> auth.uid() and not is_coach_on_client(v_uid) then return null`: for anon auth.uid() is NULL, `x <> NULL` is NULL, and the IF is never taken. Measured on PostgreSQL 16.13: the real body, run as anon with no JWT, returned another user's rows while the table showed anon none. Anon reaches it only through the default ACL (2026-06-17-source-reconcile.sql:80 grants it `to authenticated` and nothing revokes anon).
registeredFindings.notFixedHere: This change is the audit and its tripwire, and writes no migration. The only caller found, GET /api/integrations/reconcile, returns 401 before it calls the function, so no known caller needs anon. Its write twin set_metric_source has the same predicate and got the reject on 2026-06-30 (2026-06-30-rpc-authz-hardening.sql); this read twin was missed.
registeredFindings.ownerCall: Add `if auth.uid() is null then return null; end if;` as the first statement, as 2026-06-30 did for set_metric_source (create or replace with the same body, which keeps the ACL), and revoke it from anon: revoke execute on function public.get_health_sources(uuid, int) from public, anon; (authenticated stays).

registeredPinFindings.name: save_workout_session
registeredPinFindings.why: Declared after the 2026-08-09 sweep with `set search_path = public` and no pg_temp, so the sweep (a snapshot of what existed that day) never touched it and nothing has re-pinned it. The newest migration pins a different function, and that one is a trigger with security invoker.
registeredPinFindings.notFixedHere: No migration in this change. It is not anon-reachable (revoked from public and anon, granted to authenticated), so exploiting the gap needs a signed-in caller planting a relation or type in pg_temp.
registeredPinFindings.ownerCall: alter function public.save_workout_session(jsonb, jsonb, jsonb) set search_path = public, pg_temp;  (changes nothing else).
